For investors and prospective members

Assess the strategy. See the operating context.

Fish Schools bring participants together around a defined investment strategy and governance model. Fish Network is designed to connect the decisions, capital activity, and reporting that help investors evaluate how the group operates.

Participation depends on the School, its terms, availability, and eligibility requirements. It is separate from investing in Fish Network itself.

A clearer basis for participation

Understand the mandate, the authority, and the terms.

The relevant question is not simply which opportunity a School offers. It is how the group is structured to pursue it, and what information supports your assessment.

01

Mandate and strategy

Review the investment focus, portfolio approach, time horizon, and risks relevant to the proposed participation.

02

Decision rights

Establish who selects investments, who approves decisions, and which responsibilities sit with the manager, organizer, or members.

03

Economics and structure

Assess the vehicle, fees, ownership terms, liquidity restrictions, and rights attached to your participation.

04

Evidence and reporting

Examine the information supporting the group’s experience and the reporting you can expect to receive.

Beyond the presentation

Keep the reported activity connected to its source.

A report is more useful when the underlying decisions, capital activity, and supporting records can be followed. Fish Protocol is designed to preserve those connections for selected activity.

Fish Points adds proposed context about recorded contributions and participation. Access to records depends on your rights, the School’s arrangements, and the implementation.

Onchain records do not independently validate reported returns or eliminate investment risk. Participation history is not a substitute for diligence on the strategy, vehicle, and underlying evidence.
